quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When your motorcycle's weight moves forward while braking, what should you do?

options.text: You can press the front brake harder.
You should use less pressure on the front brake.
You can press the rear brake harder.
You will lose traction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can press the front brake harder.
questions.explanation: When your weight shifts forward during braking, the front wheel has more grip on the road. This means you can apply more pressure to the front brake.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking on a road with good traction, what should you do?

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and then apply it again quickly.
Release the rear brake and shift down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If the rear brake locks on a road with good traction, keep it locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle if it is upright and going straight, even with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: The center of the lane often has an oily buildup. What should you do?

options.text: Avoid it when the road is wet.
Ride only on the oily strip because it gives better grip.
Stay away from the entire center of the lane.
Do not worry about oil or other items in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid it when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars and trucks builds up in the center of lanes. When the road is dry, this strip usually has enough grip for motorcycles. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride around it and still stay in the center lane.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: At speeds faster than 55 mph.
After riding for several hours.
On short trips.
On long trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles at speeds slower than 30 mph.

questions.question: When riding through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: Look through a turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: In hot weather, should you wear a riding jacket?

options.text: Yes, it can protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration.
No, it can cause heat-related problems.
Only if the jacket is light colored.
No, it is not important.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it can protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: You should still wear a riding jacket and long pants in hot weather. They protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration, in addition to keeping you safe in a crash.

questions.question: When you are about to pass another vehicle on the left, which part of the lane should you ride in?

options.text: The left portion
The center portion
The right portion
The shoulder

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of the lane when preparing to pass. This helps you see ahead better and makes oncoming traffic more aware of you.

questions.question: Do you need hearing protection when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: No, a helmet is enough.
Yes, in addition to wearing a helmet.
Only on windy days.
No, not if you are carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, in addition to wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing even when you wear a helmet. Hearing protection lets you stay safe while still hearing important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.

options.text: always
usually
frequently
seldom

questions.correctAnswerText: seldom
questions.explanation: Riders rarely hear a tire going flat. You will notice a flat tire because the motorcycle will handle differently.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, what is the correct following distance?

options.text: One second
Two seconds
Three seconds
Four seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Four seconds
questions.explanation: You should keep at least four seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. Increase this distance when conditions are poor.

questions.question: Motorcycles are hard to see at night. What should a motorcycle rider do about this?

options.text: Ride slower at night.
Honk the horn repeatedly at night.
Do not ride at night.
Ride directly in front of other vehicles so their headlights show you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower at night.
questions.explanation: Safe night riding includes: riding slower, staying farther behind other vehicles, using the lights ahead of you to see the road, using your high beam (unless meeting or following a vehicle), and changing your lane position as needed.

questions.question: If your front wheel starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the front brake on and ride out the skid.
Keep the front brake on and release the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away, then apply it again gently.
Release the front brake and press harder on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again gently.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake completely and immediately. Then apply it smoothly again.

questions.question: What should you do before taking a long motorcycle trip?

options.text: Try to take as few rest breaks as possible.
Use caffeine or other stimulants if you feel tired.
Wear warm clothes to stay comfortable in wind, cold, and rain.
Plan to ride more than 12 hours per day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear warm clothes to stay comfortable in wind, cold, and rain.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on long trips, dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than 6 hours per day. Take a rest break at least every 2 hours. Do not use stimulants because they cause extreme fatigue when they wear off.

questions.question: Should you ride on the far side of a lane when following another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, because drivers will see you easily.
No, because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
Yes, because a passenger may tell the driver you are there.
No, because it is illegal to ride anywhere but the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
questions.explanation: Most drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane where the driver is most likely to see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Press the handlebar in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handlebar opposite the direction you want to turn.
Do not hold the handlebar because it is dangerous.
Do not lean the motorcycle because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handlebar in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: When riding faster than a walk, your motorcycle must lean to turn. Pressing the handlebar in the direction you want to turn will make the motorcycle lean the right way.

questions.question: If it starts to rain while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Ride faster.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull over to the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane has oil that makes it slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. Also, slow down on wet roads.

questions.question: When you are about to pass another rider on the left, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: In the right part of the lane so they see you in their side mirror.
In the left part of the lane to see ahead better.
In the center of the lane so they see you in their rearview mirror.
Weave in your lane to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left part of the lane to see ahead better.
questions.explanation: When passing on the left, ride in the left part of your lane to see ahead and to be more visible to drivers in the passing lane. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: The left side of the lane
The center of the lane
The right side of the lane
The best position depends on your riding conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The best position depends on your riding conditions.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best and no position should always be avoided. Choose a lane position that fits your riding conditions. It should give you enough space and make you visible to other drivers.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you tell them NOT to do?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before the engine starts.
Sit as far forward as they can without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Talk as much as they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk as much as they want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should not talk or move unnecessarily so you can focus on riding. Passengers should only get on after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold tightly to your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheel motorcycle in a group, what formation should you use?

options.text: Staggered formation.
Pyramid formation.
Single-file line.
Row of pairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file line.
questions.explanation: Staggered formations work well for two-wheel motorcycles, but three-wheel motorcycles are too wide. Groups of three-wheel motorcycles must ride in a single-file line.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle before entering a lefthand curve?

options.text: Usually ride in the right portion of the lane.
Usually ride in the left portion of the lane.
Always ride in the middle of the lane.
Always ride in the left portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually ride in the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Position yourself to see ahead clearly. For a lefthand curve, move to the right side of your lane. This helps you see oncoming traffic earlier. Adjust your position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider prevent other vehicles from sharing the lane?

options.text: Riding in the left portion of a lane.
Riding in the center portion of a lane.
Giving dirty looks if another driver moves into their lane.
Riding in a zigzag pattern to fill up a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in the center portion of a lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to prevent other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle operator do on a slippery surface?

options.text: Not use the front brake.
Make sudden moves.
Brake frequently.
Reduce their speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce their speed.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, increase your following distance, and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes together when stopping or slowing, even on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: Which type of sign is rectangular in shape?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, like speed limits, are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. You must follow the rules posted on these signs.
